notes: focusee: padding=5/25, roundness=20/20 (FocuSee's own slider units — the scenario's 40px has no conversion into that range and is clamped), shadow=0.2
focusee: the app took every channel the project declares
openscreen: MP4 export is fixed at 60 fps (MP4_EXPORT_FPS, src/cli/CliExportRunner.tsx) — which is why the pinned target is 60.

focusee: this row disagrees with the 5800X rows by a factor of nine on the same build — 10.73x here against 1.15x there, both full fidelity and verified. The machines differ in GPU, not in what was measured: an RTX 4070 Ti there, integrated Radeon graphics here. OpenScreen is 3.5x slower on this machine, which is the CPU gap; FocuSee is 24x slower, which is not. Its 467 CPU-seconds for a 208s export, over two cores held continuously, look like compositing falling back off the GPU. Published as disagreement rather than averaged, per the protocol.

conditions: measured with the desktop session in use — the Claude app and a browser held ~45% of one core throughout, on four physical cores. That is the 71-point load gap between the legs, and the reason this row is weighted x0.132. The floors themselves were steady (2.36% and 6.02% spread, drift 1.027).
